entries.answer:
Yes — Natalie can very likely destroy Realmwalker before Ace ever gets a chance to use its "cast from the top of the library" ability, because the game gives her a priority window before that ability becomes usable.

Here's the sequence. Realmwalker is a spell while it's on the stack, so it can't be "killed" (a creature-destroying effect needs a permanent creature to target) until it actually resolves and enters the battlefield [601.2a]. Once Realmwalker resolves and enters the battlefield, two things happen at once: (1) Realmwalker's own "as this creature enters, choose a creature type" instruction is applied as part of it entering, and (2) Soul Warden's ability ("Whenever another creature enters, you gain 1 life") triggers, because Realmwalker is another creature entering the battlefield. A triggered ability doesn't do anything the instant it triggers — it's put on the stack the next time a player would receive priority [117.2a]. That means before Ace can do anything else, Soul Warden's trigger goes onto the stack.

Realmwalker's permission to cast creature spells from the top of the library doesn't change when Ace is normally allowed to cast things — per its ruling, Ace can only use it at a time they could cast a sorcery: during their main phase, with the stack empty (unless something grants flash, which nothing here does) [Realmwalker ruling #3]. With Soul Warden's trigger sitting on the stack, the stack is not empty, so Ace cannot use Realmwalker's ability yet, even though Ace (as active player) gets priority first.

Ace, having nothing to do with that trigger on the stack, will have to pass priority for the game to move forward [608.1]. Once Ace passes, Natalie receives priority and can cast an instant-speed removal spell targeting Realmwalker. Because she's casting it while Soul Warden's trigger is still on the stack, her removal spell goes on top and resolves first [117.7], destroying Realmwalker before Soul Warden's trigger even resolves — and well before the stack could ever become empty again for Ace to use Realmwalker's library-casting ability.

So yes: as long as Natalie has an instant-speed way to kill Realmwalker, Soul Warden's trigger (caused by Realmwalker itself entering) creates the exact priority window she needs to act first. Note this analysis assumes a two-player game (Ace and Natalie); the provided rules don't give a multiplayer priority-passing order, so at a larger table whichever player is next after Ace in turn order would get that first response window instead, but the same core timing logic (Ace can't use Realmwalker's ability until the stack is empty) would still apply.

entries.answer_gold: Yes. When Realmwalker enters the battlefield Soul Warden's trigger will go on the stack, at which point both players will have a chance to respond.

entries.question: Nathaniel controls [Rest in Peace] and [Dauthi Voidwalker], and Armani casts [Read the Bones]. What happens to it?

After Read the Bones resolves, the rules put the card from the stack into its owner's graveyard [Armani's graveyard]. At that moment two replacement effects are both trying to modify that event: Rest in Peace's "If a card or token would be put into a graveyard from anywhere, exile it instead" (Rest in Peace text) and Dauthi Voidwalker's "If a card would be put into an opponent's graveyard from anywhere, instead exile it with a void counter on it" (Dauthi Voidwalker text) — Armani is Nathaniel's opponent, so Dauthi Voidwalker's ability qualifies too.

Since two replacement effects are attempting to modify how the same event affects the same object (the Read the Bones card), rule 616.1 says the affected object's controller — or its owner if it has no controller — chooses which one to apply [616.1]. Neither effect is a self-replacement effect and neither changes who controls an entering permanent, so those special priority steps don't force a particular choice [616.1a][616.1b]; instead any of the applicable effects may be chosen [616.1e]. The card Read the Bones is owned by Armani, so Armani makes the choice (this isn't a simultaneous multiplayer APNAP situation since only one player is choosing for this single object).

Either way, Read the Bones never reaches Armani's graveyard — it is exiled. If Armani chooses Rest in Peace's effect, it's just exiled with no counter. If Armani chooses Dauthi Voidwalker's effect, it's exiled with a void counter on it, which would let Nathaniel later tap and sacrifice Dauthi Voidwalker to play it for free. A player in Armani's position would normally pick Rest in Peace's plain exile to deny Nathaniel that option, but the choice is Armani's to make either way.

entries.question: Arely controls a [Barony Vampire]. Nico controls a [Trained Jackal]. Arely casts [Prey Upon], targeting the Barony Vampire and Trained Jackal. In response, Nico casts [Hanabi Blast], targeting the Barony Vampire. What happens?

End result: Barony Vampire is dead in Arely's graveyard (killed by Hanabi Blast, not by the fight), Trained Jackal is completely unharmed, Hanabi Blast is back in Nico's hand, and Nico has discarded one random card.

This assumes state-based actions are checked (destroying Barony Vampire) before Prey Upon resolves, which is required since state-based actions are performed before any player receives priority again after Hanabi Blast finishes resolving — there's no other plausible timing here.

entries.question: Annabel controls [Altar of Dementia] and casts [Too Greedily, Too Deep] returning Nolan's [Sepulchral Primordial] to the battlefield. Can Annabel use Altar of Dementia to sacrifice Sepulchral Primordial and return it to the battlefield using its own triggered ability?

This is an enters-the-battlefield trigger, which rule [603.6] identifies as a zone-change trigger; the most common zone-change triggers are enters-the-battlefield and leaves-the-battlefield triggers. Assuming the standard sequence — the triggered ability is put on the stack (with its target for each opponent's graveyard chosen) as soon as the spell finishes resolving, before Annabel gets priority to do anything else — Sepulchral Primordial is still sitting on the battlefield at that moment, not in any graveyard. It therefore cannot be a legal target for its own "put up to one target creature card from that player's graveyard onto the battlefield" ability at the time targets are locked in. Only after that trigger is already on the stack (with its target already fixed) does Annabel get priority to activate Altar of Dementia and sacrifice Sepulchral Primordial. Doing so sends Sepulchral Primordial to Nolan's graveyard (its owner), and under rule [400.7] it becomes a brand-new object with no connection to the permanent that just left the battlefield — but this is irrelevant to the already-stacked trigger, because that trigger's target was chosen earlier and can't be changed to point at Sepulchral Primordial now. So the sacrifice happens one step too late: it can feed Altar of Dementia's own effect ("Target player mills cards equal to the sacrificed creature's power," per Altar of Dementia's text) to mill Nolan for Sepulchral Primordial's power, but it cannot cause Sepulchral Primordial's own triggered ability to bring itself back. If instead targets for a triggered ability were chosen only when the ability resolves rather than when it's put on the stack, this loop could work — but that is not how the timing goes here, and this reasoning assumes the normal case where the trigger's target is set immediately after Too Greedily, Too Deep finishes resolving and before any player receives priority. This holds the same whether there are two players or more: Sepulchral Primordial's ability triggers "for each opponent" and picks a target from each opponent's graveyard separately at that same moment, so in a multiplayer game only the portion of the trigger aimed at Nolan's graveyard is even relevant, and it faces the identical timing problem.

entries.question: Ari casts [Memories Returning]. Does Noor have a chance to exile it with [Dawnhand Dissident] before Ari can cast Memories Returning again for its flashback cost?
entries.reason: The candidate reaches the same conclusion — Ari can cast Memories Returning with flashback before Noor gets priority to activate Dawnhand Dissident, except if Ari passes priority or a triggered ability intervenes.

Dawnhand Dissident's second ability, "{T}, Blight 2: Exile target card from a graveyard," is an activated ability, and only a player with priority may activate it ([117.1a]). Noor cannot target Memories Returning with that ability while it's still a spell on the stack — it has to actually be sitting in the graveyard first, because the ability's target is "a card from a graveyard," and a spell on the stack is not a card in a graveyard ([112.1]).

The official ruling on Memories Returning tells you exactly how the timing shakes out: once the card is in Ari's graveyard on Ari's own turn, Ari is entitled to cast it again with flashback before any other player, including Noor, gets to take any action ([Memories Returning ruling #2]). So as long as Ari immediately casts the flashback copy (paying {7}{U}{U} instead of the mana cost, per [Memories Returning ruling #4]) the moment they're able to, Noor never gets a window to activate Dawnhand Dissident against it.

The one caveat: this protection only applies if Ari actually takes the flashback-cast action right away. If Ari instead passes priority (or is somehow prevented from immediately re-casting), then priority would pass to Noor in turn, and at that point Noor could activate Dawnhand Dissident's "{T}, Blight 2: Exile target card from a graveyard" ability targeting Memories Returning while it's sitting in the graveyard, which would exile it and make it impossible for Ari to flashback it afterward. So the outcome hinges on Ari acting on their guaranteed first opportunity rather than passing priority first.

entries.answer_gold:
No. After Memories Returning resolves, Ari receives priority.. At this point, Memories Returning is in the graveyard, and they can choose to cast it again. When it's cast, it goes from the graveyard to the stack. Noor does not receive priority until after Memories Returning is on the stack, so Memories Returning can't be exiled with Dawnhand Dissident.

(Unless there's something else on the battlefield that would create a triggered ability when Memories Returning resolves. In that case, Ari wouldn't be able to cast Memories Returning until the trigger has left the stack, and Noor could exile it in response to the trigger.)

entries.question: Aubrey and Arely are playing 2HG. Aubrey attacks with [Coral Commando] and Arely casts [Flash Conscription] to gain control of Coral Commando after it's been declared as an attacker in the declare attackers step. Is it still attacking?
entries.reason: The candidate gives the same correct ruling that gaining control of the attacking creature removes it from combat (so it is no longer attacking) even in Two-Headed Giant.
entries.answer:
No. Once Arely casts Flash Conscription and gains control of Coral Commando, Coral Commando's controller changes, and rule [506.4a] states that a permanent is removed from combat if its controller changes. A creature removed from combat immediately stops being an attacking creature ([506.4], [506.4a]). So Coral Commando is no longer attacking after Flash Conscription resolves — it becomes an untapped, hasty creature under Arely's control for the rest of the turn, but it will not deal combat damage as an attacker and does not become a new attacking or blocking creature on its own.

This is true regardless of the 2HG format: the rule that a controller change removes a permanent from combat ([506.4a]) is a general combat rule that isn't altered by the Two-Headed Giant team-turn structure. (If your table were using the optional 'shared team turns' variant described in [805.10b], attackers are still declared the same way under [508.1]/[508.1k], and a mid-combat controller change would still remove the creature from combat under the same [506.4a] rule — so the outcome doesn't change between a normal two-team 2HG game and the shared-team-turns variant.)

One timing note: this assumes Flash Conscription resolves after Coral Commando has already been declared as an attacker (as the question states). If instead control changed before attackers were declared, Coral Commando simply couldn't have been declared as an attacker by Aubrey at all, since Aubrey wouldn't control it at that time.

Card data from Scryfall (scryfall.com).
entries.answer_gold: No. A creature that changes controllers is removed from combat. Even though Aubrey and Arely are on the same team and are both allowed to be attacking with creatures, they are different players and therefore Arely gaining control of Aubrey's creature still qualifies as a control change.

entries.question: Axel controls [Vastwood Gorger] and attacks Nico's [Teferi, Who Slows the Sunset]. Before damage is dealt, Nico activates [Barrin, Master Wizard], sacrificing Teferi, Who Slows the Sunset. Does Vastwood Gorger deal damage? If so, to what?
entries.reason: Both answers conclude Vastwood Gorger deals no combat damage because sacrificing the planeswalker removes the attacked object from combat so the attacker is no longer attacking anything and thus assigns no damage.
entries.answer:
Vastwood Gorger deals no combat damage at all. Sacrificing Teferi, Who Slows the Sunset removes it from the battlefield, which removes it from combat under rule [506.4c]. Since Vastwood Gorger was attacking Teferi specifically (a planeswalker, not a player), removing Teferi from combat does not remove Vastwood Gorger from combat — it remains an attacking creature, but it is no longer attacking any player, planeswalker, or battle, per [506.4c]. Vastwood Gorger has no trample or trample-over-planeswalkers ability (it's a vanilla 5/6 per its printed text), so the exception in [702.19e] for trample-over-planeswalkers creatures does not apply, and [702.19f] confirms that without that ability none of its damage can ever be redirected to the defending player even though the planeswalker it was attacking is gone. Under the combat damage assignment rules in [510.1b], an unblocked creature that isn't currently attacking anything (for example because what it was attacking left the battlefield) assigns no combat damage. So Vastwood Gorger simply deals zero damage this combat; it doesn't hit Nico, and it isn't redirected anywhere.

Note on timing: this assumes Barrin's activated ability resolves and Teferi is sacrificed before the combat damage step (i.e., 'before damage is dealt' as stated), so the removal-from-combat rules apply before damage assignment. If instead Teferi had already been removed after damage was already assigned/dealt, the outcome wouldn't change here since no damage was assigned yet in the scenario described.

entries.answer_gold: No, Vastwood Gorger does not deal any combat damage. When combat damage would be assigned, a creature that is not currently attacking anything does not deal combat damage.
